title: Hebrew
description: Modern Hebrew as spoken in Israel, written right to left with transliteration: greetings, family, food, numbers, travel, your day and shopping.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: Hebrew is written from right to left, and everyday text leaves out the vowels: 'שלום' is read shalom.
'שלום' (shalom) means hello, goodbye and peace. 'להתראות' (lehitra'ot) is see you / goodbye.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
tips: 'שלי' (sheli) means 'my' and comes after the noun: 'אמא שלי' (ima sheli) = my mother.

units.title: Food and drink
tips: 'ה' (ha-) on the front of a word means 'the': 'תה' (te) is tea, 'התה' (hate) is the tea.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
tips: Numbers have a feminine and a masculine form. For counting you use the feminine ones: אחת, שתיים, שלוש (achat, shtayim, shalosh).

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
tips: 'ל' (le-) on the front of a word means 'to': 'לשדה התעופה' (lisde hate'ufa) = to the airport.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
tips: Verbs change for men and women: a man says 'אני הולך' (ani holech), a woman 'אני הולכת' (ani holechet).

units.title: Shopping
units.description: Ask for things, prices and how to pay.
tips: 'אני רוצה' (ani rotse) means 'I want'; a woman says 'אני רוצה' too but reads it ani rotsa. Add 'בבקשה' (bevakasha) to be polite.

answers: Can I pay with a card?
Can I pay by credit card?
